P1.evidence: No setter notes were read back - the rep opened the discovery with 'I don't have a ton of info about you'. The frame covered only two of the four parts: 'dig into your story here... what you've got going on with your fitness right now, and also what it is you're looking to accomplish' - nothing on what is in the way or what he needs. Frame agreement was taken ('if that sounds good' / 'Sure. Yeah. Sounds great.') and the open question was asked verbatim in substance: 'what would you say is the biggest challenge that you're having with your fitness right now?'

P2.evidence: Age was asked but only at 00:27:24, deep into the pitch, and height was never asked; weight (172 lb) was volunteered inside a protein answer, not requested. Work was covered well, including the desk question - 'how much of your day would you say is spent working on a desk, like sitting down?' - answered 'Almost seven hours'. Health conditions were never asked. Injuries were only probed as a pitch setup ('have you noticed... that your body feels different, maybe tighter, more sore') rather than as a baseline question, and the neck stiffness and shoulder issue surfaced as a by-product. Training week, actual days trained and results from current training were all covered. Diet was raised only inside a menu question about what he would need, so the protein and vegetarian detail was volunteered. Sleep and energy were never asked at all.

P3.evidence: Strong on surface goals: 'what parts of your body right now are you primarily looking to grow?' and a 1-10 physique scale that produced a clean gap (5-6 now versus 8.5 pre-COVID). The bridge to the deeper why was asked well - 'what's going on that's got you wanting to focus on your physique and building muscle right now?' and 'why exactly are, is it important for you' - and produced confidence and self-esteem. But it stopped there. Nobody asked what he cannot physically do right now, nobody asked who else this impacts, and the drive through to husband, family, identity or longevity never happened even after he disclosed he is married. The reflect-back was about logistics ('it sounds like it's balancing your work with where you're not going super extreme') rather than 'this isn't really about the weight, it's about X'.

P4.evidence: The best-run phase. Past attempts, what happened and why it stopped were all covered, including 'why do you feel like you haven't been as consistent? Is it just the work, or is there anything else' and the direct root-cause question 'do you feel like, I mean, part of, if not the whole reason why you weren't getting results was just because you just didn't have a plan?' The prospect named the gap himself: 'Mainly, like, I didn't have a plan.' P4f ran as a weaker variant - 'is there like any particular reason why you don't just keep doing the free workouts rather than, you know, reach out to someone for help?' - which asks the question but does not land the 'information isn't the problem' frame.

P5.evidence: The Consequence Frame was not run in any form. There was no two-year question, no 'is that something you're willing to settle for', no 'why not', and no line in the sand. The rep moved straight from root cause into 'I can walk you through how that looks'. This is 20 points of weight skipped entirely and is the single largest structural failure on the call.

P6.evidence: No belief question and no all-in question were asked before presenting. The programme was presented first, and only afterwards, at 00:42:12, did the rep ask a diluted version: 'assuming that we can, like, figure out the payments and all that is, how do you feel? Do you feel like this is something you want to do?' The answer was a hedge - 'Definitely sounds interesting and kind of, like, aligns to what I'm looking for' followed by a request for a sample plan - and the rep moved forward anyway instead of returning to Phase 5 as the script requires.

P11.evidence: A close was attempted, so the phase applies. No payment was collected and no payment link was sent - the only thing exchanged was a text message to confirm phone numbers. Onboarding with Trevor, the agreement email and the Skool/welcome-email steps are all downstream of payment and were never reachable.

objection_plays.detail: Trigger was explicit: 'I'll give good thought to it and then get back to you with the decision.' The rep ran one move - the isolating question 'is it just, I guess, wanting to see the plan and what it might look like that is coming up for you? Or is there anything else?' and asked it a second time later. None of the rest ran: no 'do you feel what we've gone through CAN get you to your goal', no 'what makes you feel it can', no 'thinking isn't the problem, deciding is', no decision-identity move, no final 'are you sure, nothing else keeping you from being 100% in'. He accepted the deferral and ended the call on it.

Trigger was 'the cost of plan is, I think it's a little on the higher side'. The rep attempted the isolate - 'Is it just about the finances that you're wanting to think over? Is there like anything else that's come up for you?' - and attempted the worth-versus-afford split with 'are you saying like, whether it's worth it or if you... I the money to do it'. He never got an answer to either and never asked permission for the open financial conversation. Zero of the six financial picture questions ran: no cash on hand, no monthly surplus, no credit cards, no available credit, no investments. Instead of the play he jumped straight to a live-improvised deposit, which is the opposite sequence - the script offers to break it up only after the financial picture is on the table.

Trigger was the month-long trip to India and 'I just want to make sure I don't have anything coming up in the next six months.' The rep solved it logistically - offering to flag the month to Trevor and 'add on an extra month' - and did not run any scripted move: no 'things never slow down', no 'when does it actually become the right time', no compounding-cost frame. The prospect then rejected the workaround ('I personally would want like continuous six months'), leaving the objection alive and unaddressed.
No spousal consult was raised. The prospect disclosed he is married to a husband but never made the decision contingent on him.
No fear or doubt objection surfaced. The prospect's hesitancy was informational and comparative, not fear-based.

Two unscripted objections landed and neither has a play. First, the cheaper functioning substitute - a local in-person personal trainer plus Trevor's free Instagram content that had already produced results in three weeks. This is the known 'a cheaper alternative already worked for me' gap; the rep's response was 'there's always cheaper people out there with anything' followed by withdrawal ('I'm not here to force you to do anything... by all means'), which concedes the comparison. Second, proof-of-deliverable before purchase - the prospect asked three separate times for a sample or dummy week of programming and nutrition. The script has no answer for this and the rep deflected with a tax-planner analogy. Both are script gaps, not rep failures, and both are what he left the call to go and resolve elsewhere.

notes: The discovery front half was solid - root cause was genuinely uncovered and the prospect named his own gap - but the call collapsed structurally between P4 and the pitch: no consequence frame, no commitment check, and therefore no leverage when price and comparison objections arrived. Coach the sequence: earn the verbal yes before presenting, and never introduce a deposit figure as the first response to hesitation.
